title: The 1892 Franco-Russian military convention says it is for a defensive war against the Triple Alliance
summary: The 1892 Franco-Russian convention describes itself as a defense against a Triple Alliance attack.
body: The 1892 military convention says France and Russia have no other object than to meet the necessities of a defensive war provoked by an attack of the Triple Alliance against either of them. The text calls itself defensive. Whether the mobilization clauses later worked that way is a separate question, already argued for 1914 on another card. The wording on the page includes: "desire to preserve peace, and having no other object than to meet the necessities of a defensive war, provoked by an attack of the forces of the Triple Alliance against either of them, have agreed upon the following provisions: 1. If France is attacked by Germany, or by Italy supported by Germany, Russia shall employ all her available forces to attack Germany. If Russia is attacked by Germany, or by Austria".
